title: Goal-Oriented Ordered Autoencoding for Successive Refinement in Progressive Communication
authors: Qi Liao; Dario Bega
abstract: Goal-oriented communication often struggles to sustain downstream task performance under variable and unpredictable bandwidth. We address this problem by proposing GO-OAE (Goal-Oriented Ordered AutoEncoding), which learns a progressively refinable quantized latent sequence, optimized directly for task utility rather than source reconstruction. Each component of the sequence is represented for transmission by its code index, and the learned ordering enables inference from any received prefix of the index sequence, with performance improving as more indices arrive. We prove that optimizing the goal-oriented distortion objective is equivalent to solving a weighted conditional information bottleneck formulation, and introduce an unbiased multi-prefix importance sampling (MPIS) estimator, to reduce GO-OAE training computational cost from O(BK) to O(Bm) with m << K, and reduces the estimator variance by a factor of 1/m. Experiments show that, on MiniImageNet, GO-OAE achieves over 96% of the lossless upper-bound classification accuracy using 324 bits per image (683X compression vs. raw RGB), and already attains over 94% of the upper bound with only 70% of the transmitted indices. It consistently outperforms reconstruction-optimized codecs and ordered autoencoders trained with uniform prefix sampling across all transmission budgets, demonstrating effective communication at extreme compression rates.

title: Behavior-Mining, Generative Conversations, and Collaborative Advisory: the Future of Travel and Tourism Recommender Systems
authors: Alejandro Bellogín; Linus W. Dietz; Francesco Ricci; Pablo Sánchez
abstract: Since the early adoption of e-commerce, travel and tourism has been a lab for the design of recommender systems: tools that help travelers choose destinations, flights, accommodations, and combine them into itineraries. Data-driven recommendation techniques, ranging from case-based reasoning to reinforcement learning, have been adapted to travelers' needs. The research community has produced multifaceted prototypes of travel and tourism recommender systems (TTRSs), which are context-dependent, multistakeholder-oriented, and more recently, addressing sustainability issues, such as overtourism. Despite this enduring work, TTRSs are not widespread yet. We argue that three limitations can explain this: outdated and sparse data sets used to train and validate TTRSs, algorithms that prioritize prediction accuracy over domain-specific dimensions such as novelty and contextual relevance, and a failure to address the specific needs of travelers. Targeted incremental research could address these limitations, but a disruptive factor has meanwhile entered the ecosystem of tourism information and commercialization platforms: generative artificial intelligence. According to market research, GenAI applications are becoming the primary entry point for travelers planning their trips. This forces research to rethink how TTRSs should be designed and which core techniques should be integrated. We claim that future TTRSs, in addition to offering personalized information filtering, should become more flexible advisors that support decision making, integrating multiple data types and AI techniques, from data mining to natural language processing. Moreover, they must transparently balance the conflicting goals of travelers, service suppliers, platform owners, and local communities. We then outline research targets for building more effective TTRSs, fruitfully combining old and new recommendation techniques.

title: Mission Efficiency Optimization in Low-Altitude Economy: Adaptive Power Allocation for Coordinating Heterogeneous Aircraft Swarms
authors: Jiarui Zhang; Wei Feng; Chao Dong; Ning Ge; Qihui Wu
abstract: With the rapid development of the low-altitude economy, low-altitude operations are booming, where complex missions require collaborative efforts among multiple heterogeneous low-altitude aircrafts (LAAs). Specifically, different LAAs assume distinct roles: some for sensing, some for communication, some for computing, and others for mission execution, together forming a sensing-communication-computing-control (SC3) closed loop, akin to a reflex arc. To enable efficient coordination in such multi-LAA swarms, we introduce the concept of operational-capability entropy (OCE) to quantify the effective work capability of operational LAAs. Accordingly, by jointly considering heterogeneous OCE and channel conditions among LAAs, we formulate the power allocation problem with the goal of minimizing the linear quadratic regulator (LQR) cost, which serves as a metric for mission efficiency. The resulting complex optimization problem is decomposed into two convex subproblems that are solved iteratively, with closed-form solutions derived for each. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed mission-oriented adaptive power allocation scheme significantly outperforms traditional ones.

title: Resource-Efficient Semantic Communication for Heterogeneous Agentic Teams
authors: Farhad Rezazadeh; Hatim Chergui; Lingjia Liu; Merouane Debbah; Merouane Abdelkader Debbah
abstract: Teams of autonomous agents, including large language model (LLM) agents, must coordinate over scarce and unreliable wireless links. We propose goal-oriented semantic communication (GOSC), a closed-loop co-design that jointly decides what each agent sends, when it sends it, and how reliably it is transmitted, based on each message's value to the team task. An edge broadcast of the team's common knowledge closes the loop by updating these values. We prove that a message is sent only if its value exceeds the cost of delivering it and that more valuable messages receive more robust transmission rates, and we show that the scheduler solves each scheduling step exactly whenever the radio budget is not saturated, which held in 95% of scheduling decisions. In search-and-rescue missions validated on unseen scenarios, GOSC meets the same mission targets as carefully tuned periodic semantic schemes with 1.2--8.5 times fewer uplink channel uses. In most settings, this advantage persists with realistic packet overheads, reaching 16.6 times fewer uplink channel uses and 13.8 times lower cost when downlink costs are included; in the rescue task, it also persists when all agents share one uplink. Rough value estimates suffice, whereas values that ignore message content can fail. With three different LLMs, GOSC uses 3.2--3.5 times fewer channel uses, while completion-time gains depend on the model.

title: Semantic Map Sharing and Capability-Aware Coverage Planning for AI-Native 6G Robotic Coordination
authors: Abdulqader Dhafer; Qi Wang; Zhou Daniel Hao
abstract: Search and Rescue (SAR) operations increasingly deploy heterogeneous teams of aerial and ground robots. However, conventional coverage methods typically do not translate perceived terrain into platform-specific reachability, while continuous image exchange imposes a high communication cost. We propose an edge-centric, semantic-aware coverage planning framework that integrates aerial terrain perception, robot-specific traversability reasoning, and payload-efficient semantic state sharing. Aerial observations are converted into compact semantic grid maps, enabling reachability-constrained area decomposition and capability-aware coverage paths that assign only regions admitted by each robot's capability profile. The resulting perception-sharing-planning loop feeds semantic corrections into traversability reasoning and replanning, forming an application-level mechanism motivated by AI-enabled goal-oriented communication envisioned for AI-native 6G networks. For the high-update case, transmitting semantic corrections reduces the application payload by a factor of approximately $82$ relative to periodic full-map sharing. Across matched benchmark scenarios, the proposed method achieved $91.5\%$ coverage with no capability-infeasible allocations, compared with $78.8\%$ coverage and a $21.5\%$ capability-infeasible allocation rate for LS-MCPP. Semantic corrections update the shared planning state without requiring repeated transmission of the complete map.

title: Goal-Oriented Communication and Control Co-Design via Semantic Push-Pull in Industrial IoT
authors: Muhammad Azeem Khan; Yuriy Zacchia Lun; Aamir Mahmood; Piergiuseppe Di Marco; Mikael Gidlund; Fortunato Santucci
abstract: Emerging 6G industrial IoT architectures require wireless networked control systems capable of stabilizing diverse control loops over tightly constrained radio resources. Conventional periodic and Age-of-Information (AoI) based scheduling guarantees bounded staleness at the cost of persistent channel saturation. Conversely, pure event-triggered (PureET) strategies minimize transmissions but risk catastrophic silent deterioration when local sensor-side thresholds fail to reflect critical state evolution. To bridge this gap, we propose a communication-control co-design framework governed by a 6G Semantic Layer that independently arbitrates uplink and downlink resources. Instead of relying on freshness, our architecture evaluates the actual control impact of a packet using the state-to-error ratio (SER). We unify this control confidence with channel reliability in terms of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) to orchestrate a threshold-based sensor push and a state-aware controller pull mechanism. To ensure equitable resource allocation across dynamically heterogeneous plants, the proposed framework explicitly scales actuation deadbands according to local plant dynamics. Simulations over Rayleigh-faded channels demonstrate that this approach fundamentally shifts the Pareto frontier between transmission rate and control quality. The proposed scheme achieves tracking accuracy comparable to periodic schedulers at a reduced communication overhead, while mitigating the estimation errors characteristic of PureET.

title: Value-Based Massive Access through Goal-Oriented Irregular Repetition Slotted ALOHA
authors: Pietro Talli; Andrea Munari; Federico Mason; Federico Chiariotti; Andrea Zanella
abstract: The goal-oriented communication paradigm is poised to enable novel real-time applications by easing the burden on communication networks while still delivering task-relevant information. However, efforts so far have focused on the encoding problem, while the design of medium access schemes is still in the early stages of development, especially when connectivity is to be provided to a massive number of devices, e.g., for remote monitoring. In this respect, existing goal-oriented approaches are often centralized or based on simplified underlying mechanisms, requiring unrealistic assumptions. In this work, we present the Goal-oriented Irregular Repetition Slotted ALOHA (GO-IRSA) scheme, which combines modern random access techniques with belief-based policies. GO-IRSA does not impose significant computing loads on the sensors or require frequent feedback, and it can reduce the average and worst-case error of the estimate of a distributed Wiener process by over 30% with respect to the optimal centralized solution in a network with thousands of sensors, and is robust to imperfect interference cancellation and inaccurate process knowledge.

title: Algorithmic Justice and Responsible AI Journalism: A Comparative Communication Policy Perspective in East Asia
authors: Renxiudi Huang; Linjia Bai
abstract: As generative artificial intelligence and automated content curation rapidly reshape the global media landscape, the intersection of algorithmic justice and media governance has become a critical frontier for sustainable development. This study provides a comparative communication policy analysis of China and South Korea, focusing explicitly on how their distinct regulatory toolkits address the tension between algorithmic fairness and platform accountability in AI journalism. While China utilizes a top-down, state-centric regulatory framework emphasizing ideological security, algorithmic registration, and strict synthetic media labeling, South Korea employs a multi-stakeholder co-regulation model driven by personal data protection, anti-monopoly platform intervention, and civil society oversight. Through a detailed textual analysis of key policy documents—including China's Provisions on the Administration of Algorithmic Recommendations and South Korea's Guidelines for AI Service Ethics to Protect Users—alongside empirical evidence from prominent algorithmic news curation platforms (Toutiao and Naver), this paper evaluates the implementation efficacy and structural trade-offs of each nation's approach. We demonstrate that while both models mitigate the risks of digital infodemics and algorithmic bias, they face contrasting trade-offs between regulatory efficiency and editorial independence. Finally, this study introduces the "Policy-Media-Society" (PMS) responsive governance framework, clarifying how systemic institutional adaptations can advance UN Sustainable Development Goal 16 (SDG 16) by ensuring public access to transparent, verified information.

title: Real-Time Motion Planning: From Optimal Primitives to Cooperative Negotiation and Safety Validation
authors: Mattia Piazza
venue: Institutional Research Information System (Università degli Studi di Trento)
abstract: Autonomous vehicles represent a fundamental shift in transportation technology. They promise to improve road safety, optimize traffic flow, and increase energy efficiency. A main motivation for this change is the goal of reducing road accidents caused by human error. Meeting this goal requires vehicles that can make safe and efficient decisions in real time across the full range of conditions they encounter on the road. This ability rests on the motion planning system. A motion planner must generate dynamically feasible trajectories in complex, rapidly changing, and non-convex environments, within strict computational limits. This requirement exposes a fundamental trade-off between solution quality and computational speed. Traditional optimal control methods produce high-quality trajectories but are too slow for online use. Sampling-based methods operate faster but often yield suboptimal or infeasible maneuvers. This thesis addresses this trade-off through the concept of motion primitives, trajectory segments derived from vehicle-specific dynamic models. Motion primitives allow a planner to rapidly construct complex, dynamically feasible maneuvers, either by drawing on precomputed offline libraries or by exploiting analytical shortcuts that make their online computation fast. These primitives are integrated into the \MPTree{} framework, a modular planning architecture that combines a sampling-based search with parameterizable maneuvers. Decoupling the search strategy from maneuver generation allows the architecture to generalize across diverse driving contexts, from comfort-oriented urban navigation to time-optimal racing. The framework is then extended to multi-agent scenarios through vehicle-to-everything communication. In this setting, the planner uses communicated desired trajectories to enable decentralized, emergent negotiation among vehicles without explicit protocols, a strategy validated in simulation and on a connected vehicle platform. A high-performance planning system introduces a corresponding challenge: ensuring its safety. Traditional validation methods, such as real-world road testing, are insufficient for capturing the rare and critical events required to validate complex, optimization-based planners. This thesis addresses this challenge with a data-driven framework for safety assessment. The methodology creates a surrogate model of the autonomous system's behavior using an ensemble of bootstrapped neural networks. This model predicts safety outcomes and associated uncertainties for millions of scenarios in seconds. It enables both large-scale offline risk assessment and online risk monitoring during vehicle operation. High-performance racing places additional demands on the underlying motion primitives, requiring velocity profiles that are both time-optimal and computed at speeds suitable for online use. The Forward-Backward with Generic Acceleration (FBGA) algorithm addresses this need. FBGA computes optimal velocity profiles along fixed paths under complex, non-convex acceleration constraints. By adaptively determining acceleration and braking switching points instead of relying on apex pre-computation, it achieves accuracy comparable to offline optimal control while being up to three orders of magnitude faster. FBGA is further deployed on a physical racing platform, both as a real-time velocity replanner and as a trajectory evaluation tool within a sampling-based planner. Together, these contributions share a common methodological foundation in motion primitives, applied across complementary problems in autonomous driving: a flexible, general-purpose trajectory planner extended to cooperative multi-agent settings, a scalable methodology to validate its safety, and a fast, accurate velocity-planning algorithm for high-performance driving. This body of work contributes a set of methods toward safer and more capable autonomous driving systems.

title: Krum-Inspired Central Teacher Selection and Residual Channel Bottlenecks for Efficient DeepSC
authors: Rami Eid; Mostafa Jammoul; Omar Kaaki; Maria Slim; Mariette Awad; Hadi Sarieddeen
abstract: Deploying transformer-based semantic communication models on edge devices requires compression that preserves semantic fidelity under channel variability. We study a compressed deep semantic communication (DeepSC) student trained by multi-teacher knowledge distillation and combine two ideas: (i) a residual channel bottleneck that splits the transmitted representation into a base stream and a residual stream with unequal power allocation, and (ii) a Krum-inspired, medoid-style centrality criterion that selects a single central teacher from a five-model ensemble, applied at the logit and intermediate-feature levels and combined with a feature-dominant distillation loss. On the EuroParl benchmark, a two-layer student recovers about 98% of the four-layer teacher's bilingual evaluation understudy (BLEU)-1 under additive white Gaussian noise, with 93% of its BLEU-4 and 96% of its sentence-BERT (SBERT) score, and about 89%, 77%, and 87% of the teacher's BLEU-1, BLEU-4, and SBERT, respectively, under Rayleigh fading, while reducing non-embedding parameters by 1.33x and single-teacher inference latency by 1.79x (9.0x relative to a five-teacher ensemble used here as an upper-bound reference, not a deployment baseline). Controlled ablations over three seeds indicate complementary contributions of about +8.4% BLEU-1 (+9.6% SBERT) from the residual bottleneck and +3.0% (+2.9% SBERT) from centrality-based selection over mean aggregation. A decoder-mode ablation shows that the base stream alone recovers about two-thirds of the full BLEU-1 while the residual stream alone collapses, supporting the role of the residual as a refinement on top of the base.

title: Where to Defend? Layer-Wise Adversarial Training for Robust Transformer-Based Semantic Communications
authors: Maria Slim; Razane Tajeddine; Mariette Awad; Hadi Sarieddeen
abstract: Deep learning-based semantic communication (DeepSC), a Transformer-based encoder-decoder, achieves semantic fidelity over noisy channels but remains vulnerable to adversarial perturbations injected at multiple stages of the pipeline. We present a layer-wise robustness framework that compares fast gradient sign method (FGSM), projected gradient descent (PGD), and l2-normalized fast gradient method (FGM) defenses at the embedding output, and then uses PGD to analyze three attack and defense points: the embedding output, encoder output, and channel-encoder bottleneck. We evaluate reconstruction on Europarl and UK Hansard and sentiment classification on SST2 and YELP under additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and Rayleigh fading. A first-order damage budget, {epsilon} times the l1 norm of the clean-input loss gradient at each injection point, predicts the attack-severity ordering, and the transfer matrix reveals asymmetric defense transfer: the embedding defense transfers strongly to encoder attacks, whereas encoder defenses degrade robustness against upstream attacks. For reconstruction, encoder-point training yields the largest matched gain but fails severely under embedding attacks; joint embedding-plus-encoder training retains comparable gains under encoder attacks while mitigating this mismatch failure, and Rayleigh fading attenuates robustness gains and degradation. For classification, three of four defenses collapse to constant predictors; only the channel-encoder defense remains non-degenerate, suggesting a protective role for the 128D-to-16D bottleneck. At a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 9 dB and perturbation budget {epsilon} = 0.3, the matched encoder defense recovers bilingual evaluation understudy (BLEU) from ~ 0.10 to ~ 0.64 on Europarl/AWGN, whereas the mismatched encoder defense yields a -0.444 BLEU change relative to the undefended baseline under an embedding attack.

title: Semantic-Aware Sub-Band Allocation for Terahertz Communications
authors: Fatima Ismail; Hadi Sarieddeen; Jihad Fahs
abstract: This paper studies semantic-aware sub-band al- location for terahertz (THz) communication systems, where frequency-selective molecular absorption creates highly non- uniform sub-band qualities. Unlike conventional formulations, semantic fidelity depends nonlinearly on the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and is also sentence-specific, leading to a non-separable assignment problem that is generally not solvable using simple ordering-based policies. To address this, we use a sentence-BERT (SBERT)-based surrogate model that predicts semantic fidelity from the sentence embedding and sub-band SNR. We propose an importance-aware scheduler that assigns sentences to sub- bands based on their semantic contribution using an oracle utility function that captures importance-weighted semantic similarity across sentence-sub-band pairs. A neural scheduler is then trained through imitation learning to approximate the oracle policy at more than 200x lower runtime than full DeepSC- based oracle evaluation. Integrated with a deep-learning-enabled semantic communication (DeepSC) system, the proposed method consistently outperforms all benchmark schemes and approaches oracle-level performance under realistic THz channel conditions.

title: Flexible Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding: A Vibrotactile Example
authors: Shuijie Li; Kemi Chen; Runjie Wang; Tiesong Zhao; Xiaoming Tao
abstract: The increasing demand for real-time tactile communication in multimedia systems has exposed the limitations of existing Joint Source-Channel Coding (JSCC) techniques. While current JSCC models facilitate end-to-end optimization, they typically operate at fixed coding rates and require separate model instances for different rate settings. This results in significant storage overhead and limited adaptability to dynamic bandwidth conditions. To address these challenges, we propose the Flexible Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding (FD-JSCC) framework for vibrotactile signals, which supports flexible-rate transmission without the need for model switching. The FD-JSCC integrates a flexible-rate encoder-decoder enhanced with Hierarchical Gain Adaptation Module (HGAM) and Rate-Switchable Residual Module (RSRM), enabling bitrate-aware compression by selectively preserving salient vibrotactile features. Additionally, we introduce a Channel Feature Processing Module (CFPM), which leverages real-time SNR information to enhance robustness against channel noise and signal degradation. Trained on the IEEE 1918.1.1 vibrotactile dataset, FD-JSCC achieves reconstruction performance comparable to fixed-rate baselines (e.g., DeepSC-S), while reducing storage requirements by 61.1\% when supporting four rates. These results underscore its potential for scalable, low-latency tactile communication in next-generation networks.

title: Compressibility is not Feedback: A Random-access Gap in Causal Semantic Repair
authors: Milad Bafarassat
abstract: Semantic feedback can repair a noisy first decode without retransmitting the whole message, but current end-to-end evaluations hide where a feedback design fails. An oracle that sees both the source-side state and receiver observation may describe a useful correction with few bits, while the receiver, which sees only its own observation, may not know which correction to request. We formulate these as distinct direct and receiver-constrained coding problems, connect repair distortion to retained local utility and prove a random-access separation: one direct bit is exact although receiver utility vanishes with the number of source-conditioned alternatives. A synthetic ladder verifies the exact law. In paired populations of eight Reuters text-JSCC codecs, the trained recurrent population retains over three times more direct 16-bit repair value than the trained DeepSC population despite comparable full-repair opportunity. Nevertheless, an entropy-valid receiver audit across all eight recurrent checkpoints does not resolve against repetition, source-only or shuffled-index controls. The results show that compressible repair is an upper bound, not evidence of deployable feedback, and motivate reporting both rate curves under matched resources.

title: SignDeepSC: A Semantic Signature-based Approach for Robust Semantic Communication
authors: Khalil Alhaj; Razane Tajeddine; Hadi Sarieddeen
abstract: Semantic communication systems such as deep semantic communication (DeepSC) offer high efficiency but are vulnerable to adversarial attacks on their underlying neural networks. We address a physical-layer man-in-the-middle (MitM) threat in which an adversary injects perturbations into the transmitted signal to distort its meaning. We propose SignDeepSC, an architectural defense that achieves adversarial robustness without requiring explicit adversarial example generation during training. The approach is built on a perceiver-inspired semantic signature, a compact vector summary of the source features transmitted over a separate low-rate auxiliary channel. This signature is used by a self-repairing decoder that leverages cross-attention to correct distortions and can additionally drive a scrambler that shuffles the feature layout. We evaluate SignDeepSC over Rayleigh fading and additive white Gaussian noise channels under both single-step fast gradient sign method (FGSM) and iterative projected gradient descent (PGD) attacks. Under PGD ($ε= 0.7$), at 12~dB signal-to-noise ratio with Rayleigh fading, SignDeepSC achieves a bilingual evaluation understudy (BLEU-4) score of 0.237 and bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (BERT) sentence similarity of 0.646, outperforming all baselines without degrading clean-channel performance, when the signature channel is well protected.

title: Structured Spectral Compression based Low-Bitrate Secure Speech Communications for Internet of Things assisted Non-Terrestrial Networks
authors: Li Ping Qian; Zhehan Chen; Qianru Wang; Qian Wang; Yuan Wu; Xuemin Sherman Shen
abstract: This paper focuses on the Low-Bitrate Secure Speech Communications based on the Structured Spectral Compression (LB-S2C2). Specifically, the Mel spectral matrix of the speech signal is first encoded at the transmitter side through compressive sensing based on waveform segmentation and data quantization. Then, the Automatic Repeat Request (ARQ) is combined with forward error correction to achieve reliable transmission of speech signals over wireless channels. Thirdly, the received signals are recovered as the speech at the receiver side. Finally, we conduct a series of simulation experiments for the performance evaluation of LB-S2C2. Our simulations reveal that the dictionary matrix used for the speech reconstruction is different from the one used for the high-order matrix sparsification by even only approximately 0.1%, and then the accurate speech recovery fails. It implies that the speech data can be securely transmitted when the dictionary matrix is preserved. More importantly, the LB-S2C2 exhibits a very high privacy protection capability with the average voiceprint similarity to be only 0.3, which is much lower than the 0.8 of the semantic speech communication scheme DeepSC-S, and even lower than the 0.33 of the latest speech communication scheme OFI-OFCNB. In addition, our simulations reveal that the proposed structured speech coding boasts a time complexity of merely O(n), and the proposed speech recovery scheme requires the 12-bit memory storage only, which outperforms the traditional encryption algorithms proposed for speech communications. In comparison with the conventional compression techniques, our spectral compression method renders the coding rate of only 3.9kbps, which is lower than the current lowest speech coding rate of 6.3kbps achieved by G.723.

title: Semantic Communications in the THz Band
authors: Fatima Ismail; Hadi Sarieddeen; Jihad Fahs
abstract: Semantic and terahertz (THz)-band communications are algorithmic and spectral enablers of future wireless networks. This work investigates deep learning-based semantic communication (DeepSC) over THz channels. We show that DeepSC models trained solely under additive white Gaussian noise generalize well to the tested THz block- and fast-fading channels when receiver-side compensation is applied. To enable fully data-driven reception, we propose a lightweight neural detector that does not require channel state information (CSI). At 0.3 THz, DeepSC outperforms a throughput-matched traditional coded communication system baseline over 0-12 dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), achieving more than 50 percentage-point higher Bilingual Evaluation Understudy unigram (BLEU-1) score. The proposed pilot-free detector outperforms minimum mean square error (MMSE) equalization with both perfect and imperfect CSI and remains robust to frequency offsets up to 50 MHz, highlighting the resilience of semantic communication to THz channel impairments.

title: Image Semantic Communication with Quadtree Partition-based Coding
authors: Yinhuan Huang; Zhijin Qin
abstract: Deep learning based semantic communication (DeepSC) system has emerged as a promising paradigm for efficient wireless transmission. However, existing image DeepSC methods, frequently encounter challenges in balancing rate-distortion performance and computational complexity, and often exhibit inferior performance compared to traditional schemes, especially on high-resolution datasets. To address these limitations, we propose a novel image DeepSC system, using quadtree partition-based joint semantic-channel coding, named Quad-DeepSC, which maintains low complexity while achieving state-of-the-art transmission performance. Based on maturing learned image compression technologies, we establish a unified DeepSC system design and training pipeline. The proposed Quad-DeepSC integrates quadtree partition-based entropy estimation and feature coding modules with lightweight feature extraction and reconstruction networks to form an end-to-end architecture. During training, all components except the feature coding modules are jointly optimized as a compact learned image codec, Quad-LIC, for source compression tasks. The pretrained Quad-LIC is then embedded into Quad-DeepSC and fine-tuned end-to-end over wireless channels. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that Quad-DeepSC is the first DeepSC system to surpass conventional communication systems, which employ VTM for source coding and adopt the optimal MCS index under 3GPP standards for channel coding and digital modulation, in performance across datasets of varying resolutions. Notably, both Quad-DeepSC and Quad-LIC exhibit minimal latency, rendering them well-suited for deployment in real-time wireless communication systems.

title: VQ-VAE Based Digital Semantic Communication with Importance-Aware OFDM Transmission
authors: Ming Lyu; Hao Chen; Dan Wang; Chen Qiu; Guangyin Feng; Nan Ma; Xiaodong Xu
abstract: Semantic communication (SemCom) significantly reduces redundant data and improves transmission efficiency by extracting the latent features of information. However, most of the conventional deep learning-based SemCom systems focus on analog transmission and lack in compatibility with practical digital communications. This paper proposes a vector quantized-variational autoencoder (VQ-VAE) based digital SemCom system that directly transmits the semantic features and incorporates the importance-aware orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) transmission to enhance the SemCom performance, where the VQ-VAE generates a discrete codebook shared between the transmitter and receiver. At transmitter, the latent semantic features are firstly extracted by VQ-VAE, and then the shared codebook is adopted to match these features, which are subsequently transformed into a discrete version to adapt the digital transmission. To protect the semantic information, an importance-aware OFDM transmission strategy is proposed to allocate the key features near the OFDM reference signals, where the feature importance is derived from the gradient-based method. At the receiver, the features are rematched with the shared codebook to further correct errors. Finally, experimental results demonstrate that our proposed scheme outperforms the conventional DeepSC and achieves better reconstruction performance under low SNR region.

title: Resource optimization for RIS-UAV integrated air-ground cooperative semantic communication driven by deep reinforcement learning
authors: Yufei Dai; Yuanyuan Yao; Sai Huang; Xinwei Yue
abstract: To meet the 6G semantic transmission requirements, this paper proposes an air-ground dual-mode semantic transmission architecture for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS)-aided Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) networks. By dynamically assigning RIS-reflected links to users with long packets and direct UAV line-of-sight (LOS) links to users with short packets, we jointly optimize semantic symbols, RIS phase shifts, UAV three-dimensional (3D) trajectory, and transmit power to maximize the system-level semantic Quality of Experience (QoE). To efficiently solve the formulated non-convex mixed-integer optimization problem, we present an Action Space Decoupled Hybrid Deep Reinforcement Learning (ASD-HDRL) framework, which employs the Dueling Double Deep Q-Network (D3QN) for discrete semantic resource decision-making and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) for continuous control optimization. Simulation results verify that the proposed ASD-HDRL achieves superior system-level semantic QoE performance.

title: QoE-Driven Hybrid Resource Allocation for Multi-User OFDMA Semantic Communications
authors: Xiaotian Xu; Zhifeng Tang; Guangchen Wang; Nan Yang; Xiangyun Zhou; Salman Durrani; Yansha Deng
abstract: In this paper, we develop a quality-of-experience (QoE)-driven hybrid resource allocation framework for multi-user downlink orthogonal frequency-division multiple access semantic communication systems, where the hybrid framework jointly handles continuous and discrete decision variables. Specifically, we formulate a mixed continuous-discrete optimization problem to jointly optimize transmit power, subcarrier allocation, and semantic decisions under coupled power and spectrum constraints. To better characterize semantic service quality, we propose a preference-inverse multiplicative exponential QoE that is bounded and non-compensatory, capturing the intrinsic ``both-required'' property of semantic rate and similarity. To solve the optimization problem, we develop a projection-based multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient framework that enforces feasibility for continuous and discrete actions. Furthermore, we integrate Gumbel-softmax relaxation with an adaptive performance-driven temperature annealing scheme to enhance the learning of discrete semantic decisions. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed framework achieves superior convergence, greater stability, and higher QoE compared to the conventional QoE design and penalty-based or fixed-temperature baselines, highlighting the benefits of our QoE design and the effectiveness of hybrid decision learning in semantic communications.

title: Guess and Send: World-Model-Guided Semantic Packet Transmission for Robust Video Perception
authors: Yan Gong; Zheng Chu; Wei Koong Chai; Hari Mohan Pandey; Jiankang Zhang; Jingrui Hou; Miao Zhang; Y. Li; Pei Xiao; Yuanjian Li
abstract: Reliable video perception over bandwidth-constrained wireless links requires transmitting information that the receiver cannot already recover from its evolving scene representation. This paper introduces WorldGT, a world-model-guided semantic packet transmission framework that prioritizes information according to its contribution to the receiver's perception. A shared feature-space world model predicts the receiver's scene state through affine motion compensation and learned residual displacement, while sender-side verification identifies reusable predictions. An acknowledgment-synchronized receiver twin estimates task-impact scores through two counterfactual evaluations, guiding packet selection and unequal error protection over LDPC-coded wireless channels. A compact 3-bit feature representation increases spatial coverage under stringent bandwidth constraints, while predictive fallback sustains perception during packet outages. Experiments on KITTI and VisDrone under Rayleigh fading and AWGN demonstrate substantial gains in low-SNR conditions. On KITTI at a 4.13% reference bandwidth budget, WorldGT achieves 47.5% J&F at 0 dB Rayleigh SNR, outperforming H.264 by 11.3 percentage points. Controlled ablations show that world-model prediction contributes up to 8.7 points under Rayleigh fading. Object-detection experiments further demonstrate the transferability of receiver-relative predictive transmission across visual perception tasks. These results establish world-model-guided, receiver-state-aware transmission as an effective approach to robust video perception under severe communication constraints.
keywords: DeepSC; semantic-aware communication; semantic channel coding

title: AI-ENABLED SEMANTIC COMMUNICATION ARCHITECTURE FOR 6G NETWORKS: AN INTELLIGENT, CONTEXT-AWARE AND RESOURCE-EFFICIENT FRAMEWORK WITH HYBRID OPTIMIZATION
authors: Ganesan S.; Jagatheeshkumar G.
venue: International Journal of Science and Research Archive
abstract: Communication architectures that can enable intelligent services, vast connectivity, ultra-low latency, and extremely heterogeneous applications are necessary due to the sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks' rapid expansion. Large amounts of redundant data are communicated with significant bandwidth, energy, and computational overhead since conventional communication systems are primarily concerned with correct bit-level transmission. By conveying task-relevant meaning rather than full raw data, semantic communication overcomes this constraint. This research presents an AI-Enabled Semantic Communication Architecture for 6G Networks that combines context-aware decision-making, intelligent semantic extraction, and hybrid optimization. Gray Wolf Optimization (GWO) optimizes transmission parameters and semantic reconstruction quality, whereas Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) selects semantic features and allocates communication resources in the suggested framework. The optimization method is dynamically modified by a context-aware semantic controller based on network resources, channel conditions, and application needs. The framework is intended to maximize semantic similarity and communication efficiency while minimizing semantic distortion, latency, energy usage, and bandwidth utilization. Text-based semantic communication is used in an experimental assessment framework with different network loads and signal-to-noise ratios. For upcoming 6G applications, the suggested architecture offers a basis for resource-efficient, flexible, and intelligent semantic communication.

title: Multi-Source and Multi-Dimensional Information Fusion in Resource-Constrained Edge Networks
authors: Yushi Wang; Zhengxin Yu; Guhan Zheng; Wang Miao; Merouane Abdelkader Debbah
abstract: Multi-source semantic information fusion enables edge networks to support global inference using observations collected by distributed terminals. However, limited communication and computation resources restrict semantic uploading, leaving the edge server with incomplete tokens that differ in modality, semantic granularity, arrival time, and channel condition. The value of these tokens also depends on the complementary or redundant information provided by other terminals. In this paper, we propose a multi-source and multi-dimensional semantic information fusion framework that coordinates terminal uploading and edge-side fusion under resource constraints. We develop Hyper-Slot to combine semantic content with available token attributes through iterative token-to-slot assignment and slot-to-token feedback, producing a compact representation for global inference. To encourage useful semantic uploading, we further design a contribution-based incentive mechanism that uses Hyper-Slot assignments to evaluate information coverage and cross-type complementarity. A bi-level Stackelberg-Nash game determines the server reward pool and terminal transmission-quality strategies while accounting for computation and communication energy costs. Experiments on a tri-modal extension of COCO2014 and image-text retrieval on Flickr30K show that Hyper-Slot improves mAP by 3.66 percentage points and RSum by 15.9 points over the strongest evaluated baselines, respectively, while reducing the number of parameters by more than 80% compared with a naive concatenation-based fusion baseline.

title: Adaptive Goal-Oriented Semantic Communication with Pretrained Semantic Encoding and Effectiveness-Aware Equalization for Beyond-5G/6G Networks
authors: Haseeb Ur Rehman; Kashif Bashir; Afzal Shah Muhammad; Suleman Soomro Muhammad; Umar Shahzad Khan Muhammad; Nouman Bashir
abstract: Semantic communication seeks to transmit task-relevant meaning rather than reproduce every source bit, but learned semantic representations can deteriorate sharply when they are perturbed by channel noise. This paper presents an adaptive, goal-oriented semantic communication framework that combines a pretrained Sentence-BERT (SBERT) encoder with a noise-conditioned neural equalizer. Text is mapped to a 384-dimensional semantic vector, perturbed by additive white Gaussian noise, and processed by the equalizer only when the estimated noise standard deviation exceeds an activation threshold of τ=0.05. A cosine-similarity rule then determines whether the recovered representation is accepted or sent for refinement or retransmission. In the reported embedding-domain experiments, adaptive equalization increased mean semantic similarity from 0.2475 to 0.6303 at σ=0.20 and from 0.0740 to 0.3545 at σ=0.70. The corresponding absolute gains were 0.3828 and 0.2805, respectively. At σ≤0.05, the equalizer was bypassed and produced no measurable change, avoiding unnecessary correction under mild perturbations. These results establish a proof of concept for noise-triggered recovery of pretrained semantic embeddings.

title: Collective Emergent Alignment: Measuring and Amplifying Interaction-Induced Reasoning Alignment in Multi-Agent LLMs
authors: Boxuan Wang; Zhuoyun Li; Sarvapali D. Ramchurn; Xiaowei Huang; Yi Dong
abstract: Multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems can exhibit emergent behaviors through interaction, yet whether a similar phenomenon exists for reasoning alignment remains largely unexplored. We study whether agent interaction produces additional reference-grounded reasoning alignment beyond matched individual self-refinement, and introduce REMAP (Reference-Entailment-Matrix for Agentic Process), a framework that quantifies this effect through Semantic Coverage and interaction-specific alignment gains. Across diverse model families and two multi-hop reasoning benchmarks, we observe broadly positive interaction gains, particularly on reasoning content that depends on integrating evidence distributed across agents. These gains are consistently associated with independently measured peer-information recovery, while further analysis reveals composition-dependent heterogeneity effects and asymmetric information transfer across agent capability levels. Motivated by these findings, we further introduce a fact-level multi-agent communication framework that replaces full reasoning-trace exchange with compact, gap-aware, and selectively routed information. Our experiments show that compact fact exchange improves reasoning alignment and task performance while reducing communication overhead, whereas more selective communication exposes a trade-off between acquiring distributed information, retaining local content, and communication efficiency. Overall, our results show that collective emergent alignment can be quantified, linked to information-transfer patterns, and used to guide more effective multi-agent communication.

title: Multi-view Semantic-aware Resource Allocation for Edge AI
authors: Jiawei Luo; Hussein Saleh; Mohamad Assaad
abstract: Semantic communication is emerging as a pivotal paradigm to overcome wireless resource scarcity in 6G networks. This paper proposes a novel end-to-end framework for semantics-aware resource allocation in multi-user Edge AI. We extend the Opportunistic Information Bottleneck (OIB) to a multi-view setting, termed the Multi-view Gaussian Information Bottleneck (MGIB), by fusing complementary source views without variational approximation or network retraining. A resource allocation framework is then formulated for joint compression-level selection, transmission mode selection (i.e., the number of active sources per group), and PRB assignment. The problem is formulated as a Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP), solved efficiently via a proposed Lagrangian Relaxation (LR) algorithm, and benchmarked against the NP-hard optimal solution. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed LR scheme achieves near-optimal utility, and doubles PRB efficiency versus average allocation.

title: SEMPRE: Semantic-Aware Protocol Reverse Engineering via Consistency-Driven Joint Optimization
authors: Yihua Xu; Weijie Huang; Xiaofeng Wang; Hang Zhang; Binghui Wang; Yue Duan
abstract: Protocol reverse engineering (PRE) is essential for understanding undocumented or proprietary communication formats, enabling security-critical tasks such as vulnerability discovery, malware C2 analysis, and IDS signature generation. However, existing PRE techniques rely on brittle hand-written rules, under-model contextual dependencies among neighboring fields, and often fail on messages with nested sub-protocols. We present SEMPRE, a fully automated PRE framework that replaces ad-hoc heuristics with recursive LLM reasoning grounded in fine-grained dynamic program analysis. SEMPRE uses taint-flow and loop traces to guide an LLM-driven tree-of-thought search that slices messages into fields while detecting nested sub-payloads, producing a hierarchical layout. It then infers each field's type and role and iteratively refines boundaries by freezing high-confidence segments and re-running detection under semantic constraints, yielding an EM-style procedure that monotonically improves structure and semantics until convergence. Evaluated on a broad corpus of mainstream protocols against six state-of-the-art (vs. <0.4 for all baselines) and 0.72 for semantic inference (vs. 0.13 for BinPRE). Ablations confirm the contribution of each component, and a case study on a prolific real-world botnet demonstrates practical utility.

title: LAST-V2X: Language-Driven Adaptive Scenario Synthesis and Testing for Communication-Induced Failures in V2X Safety Applications
authors: Keshu Wu; Hao Zhang; Rui Gan; Pei Li; Jiwan Jiang; Yang Zhou
abstract: Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication enables connected vehicles to make safety-critical decisions, but delayed, missing, or incorrect information can compromise driving safety. Systematically testing such failures is challenging because traffic interactions, communication conditions, and application responses must be jointly configured to produce meaningful scenarios. This paper presents LAST-V2X, a language-driven, adaptive framework for automated scenario synthesis and safety testing of V2X applications. LAST-V2X leverages large language models (LLMs) to translate natural-language test descriptions into executable scenarios grounded in roadway geometry, V2X communication semantics, and vehicle behavior. The framework integrates physical traffic simulation with spatially aware communication modeling and message-level fault injection to evaluate how information degradation affects vehicle decisions. To establish whether an observed safety failure is caused by communication rather than the underlying traffic conditions, LAST-V2X employs matched executions under degraded and ground-truth information. Furthermore, an execution-guided refinement mechanism combines parameter search and LLM self-reflection to identify ineffective test configurations, improve scenario effectiveness, and produce minimal reproducible failure cases. Experiments across diverse CARLA environments and V2X safety applications demonstrate the framework's ability to generate reliable scenarios, distinguish communication-induced failures from unrelated safety violations, and substantially improve failure discovery through adaptive refinement. These results establish LAST-V2X as a systematic approach to language-driven, causally verified, and adaptive safety testing for connected vehicle systems.

title: Beyond Task Relevance: Interaction-Aware Semantic Communication for Wireless Agent Collaboration
authors: Yiru Wang; Pengxin Guan; Xiumei Deng; Zehui Xiong
abstract: Semantic communication in multi-agent systems often assumes that task-relevant information benefits the team once delivered. Yet semantic sharing can alter the receiver's decision and increase inter-agent dependence, potentially reducing team utility. Motivated by this phenomenon, we develop an interaction-aware framework for wireless collaboration between heterogeneous agents. We analytically relate communication-induced dependence to expected best-of-team utility and define a team-level semantic value for candidate messages. We consider semantic units at different abstraction levels and formulate a deadline- and power-constrained problem that maximizes predicted team-level net surplus. We derive an interaction-aware policy that selects at most one unit and its transmit power, or chooses not to transmit. Experiments on two verifier-scored optimization tasks show that full-solution exchange induces stronger structural convergence and more adverse team-level effects, whereas method hints exhibit pronounced directionality. Across the evaluated power budgets, our policy achieves the highest net team-level surplus while consuming less energy than semantic-aware and full-solution baselines.

title: Towards High Semantic Fidelity: Hyperdimensional Symbolic Messages in Multi-Agent Communication
authors: Shoucheng Song; Chang Yao; Hao Wu; Youfang Lin; Sheng Han; Kai Lv
abstract: Semantic fidelity is essential for multi-agent communication under non-ideal channels, comprising transmission fidelity and conversion fidelity. Yet existing numerical and neural message formats cannot simultaneously achieve both. To address this, we propose a novel message format-\textbf{H}yperdimensional \textbf{S}ymbolic \textbf{M}essages (HSM) and its corresponding communication framework \textbf{Herm}. For transmission fidelity, Herm suppresses semantic entanglement via an entity-attribute-value structured encoding pipeline. For conversion fidelity, Herm first leverages a receiver-centric ego-binding mechanism to align semantics. Then, a similarity-aware dual-branch fusion module is proposed to prevent critical semantic dilution. To realize explicit message-semantic conversion, we devise an iterative decoding scheme via algebraic inverse operations. Experiments exhibit that Herm outperforms baselines across various noisy scenarios while maintaining superior structural readability.

title: Cryptographically Secure Agent-to-Agent Communication in Multi-Agent Systems
authors: Karol Budzyn; Adrian Brodzik; Mateusz Szczepkowski
abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) comprise AI agents that collaborate or compete to perform complex, distributed tasks. Their dynamic interactions create opportunities for threat actors to target and impersonate other agents, intercept messages, inject malicious prompts, and exfiltrate sensitive data while simultaneously complicating the detection of anomalous behavior through conventional monitoring. This paper surveys threats and cryptographic challenges in agent-to-agent communication and presents a zero-trust architecture integrating identity, transport security, message integrity, and monitoring. The architecture establishes agent identities via decentralized identifiers and task-scoped verifiable credentials backed by a permissioned ledger, enforcing least-privilege authorization. For transport security, it provides mutually authenticated, crypto-agile TLS with hybrid post-quantum key establishment, and evaluates KEMTLS with pre-distributed public keys to reduce handshake overhead. Signed CBOR envelopes preserve payload integrity across multi-hop exchanges, while zero-knowledge proofs verify declared task constraints without exposing underlying inputs. Context-aware monitoring of inter-agent messages, tool activity, and execution telemetry informs the setting of risk-based trust thresholds and supports the detection of behavioral anomalies. Together, these mechanisms provide an integrated framework for securing and auditing agent communication, with implications for other agentic protocols and prospective 6G semantic communication.

title: Factors Affecting a Curriculum Based on Citizenship Legal Literacy Education
authors: Kobra Gholizadeh Chennab; Shahram Ranjdoust
venue: International Journal of Education and Cognitive Sciences
abstract: Purpose: This study aimed to identify the factors affecting a curriculum based on citizenship legal literacy education in order to improve the quality of civic education in Iran’s educational system. Methods and Materials: This applied and developmental study was conducted using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. In the qualitative phase, the statistical population included experts in education, curriculum planning, social sciences, and citizenship rights. Participants were selected through purposive and snowball sampling. Data were collected through 15 semi-structured interviews, which continued until theoretical saturation was achieved. The qualitative data were analyzed using MaxQDA software through open, axial, and selective coding. The extracted themes were then organized to develop a conceptual structure for a curriculum based on citizenship legal literacy education. Findings: The inferential findings supported a multidimensional structure for citizenship legal literacy education. The analysis indicated that five key components formed the core of the proposed curriculum model: citizenship rights education, values and beliefs, practical empowerment, development of social interaction, and media and digital literacy education. These components represented interrelated knowledge-based, attitudinal, behavioral, and social indicators. The findings showed that emphasis on citizens’ rights and responsibilities, justice-oriented attitudes, dialogue skills, social participation, legal awareness, responsible media use, and digital literacy plays a decisive role in designing an effective curriculum for educating law-abiding and participatory citizens. Conclusion: The results suggest that citizenship legal literacy education in Iran requires a shift from the mere transmission of theoretical concepts toward a competency-based, participatory, and practice-oriented curriculum. Such a curriculum can contribute to strengthening civic awareness, promoting legal responsibility, enhancing social participation, supporting educational justice, and preparing students for active and responsible citizenship in contemporary society.

title: Designing an Educational Planning Model Based on the Agricultural Value Chain with a Qualitative Approach
authors: Bentolhoda Ramezanzadeh; Hamidreza Arasteh; Kamran Mohammadkhani; Abbasali Motalebi
venue: Future of Work and Digital Management Journal
abstract: Educational planning based on the agricultural value chain, as a comprehensive and systematic approach, can make a substantial contribution to improving quality and productivity in the agricultural sector. Therefore, the aim of the present study was to design an educational planning model based on the agricultural value chain in citrus orchards in northern Iran. This study is classified as qualitative grounded-theory research. The statistical population consisted of 20 experts and faculty members of the Agricultural Research, Education and Extension Organization. Interviews were used for data collection, and MAXQDA 2020 software was employed for data analysis. The findings identified the research components, including causal conditions consisting of core content, educational activities, and supplementary programs; the central phenomenon, namely educational programs based on the agricultural value chain; contextual factors including macro-level policies and culture; intervening factors including evaluation, core policies, competition, and educational approaches; strategies including organizational strategies and environmental strategies; and outcomes including optimal value chain management, quality orientation, and educational enhancement.

title: Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis of Fashion and Apparel Related Reviews using Transformer Model
authors: Foud Ameri; Ghasem Bakhshandeh; Maryam Darvishi
venue: Journal of Management and Business Solutions
abstract: The increasing reliance on e-commerce has led to a surge in customer-generated content, making sentiment analysis a crucial tool for understanding consumer preferences. This study presents a novel aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) approach to extract fine-grained insights from customer reviews across multiple product categories, including lingerie, women’s clothing, men’s clothing, kids’ apparel, home & furniture, and flowers & plants. We employ exploratory data analysis (EDA) to uncover key patterns in customer sentiment and utilize a transformer-based model with contrastive learning to enhance sentiment classification accuracy. Our approach effectively captures sentiment variations across nine different aspects, including quality, value for money, style, fit, material, warmth, comfort, support, and how well the product fits. The results demonstrate that our model outperforms traditional sentiment analysis methods, offering a more structured understanding of customer feedback. By analyzing customer sentiments from reviews, businesses can identify dissatisfaction patterns that may contribute to customer churn. Addressing these issues proactively can help improve customer retention and loyalty. These insights can help businesses refine their product offerings and improve customer satisfaction across diverse e-commerce categories.

title: Semantic-Assisted Joint Channel Estimation and Symbol Detection for MU-MIMO Systems
authors: Hao Chang; Chentao Yue; Haiyao Yu; Yonghui Li; Branka Vucetic; Wibowo Hardjawana
abstract: This paper presents a semantic-assisted joint channel estimation and symbol detection (Sem-JCED) receiver framework for text transmission in multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) systems. Sem-JCED integrates a linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE) channel estimator, an expectation propagation (EP) symbol detector, and a semantic corrector based on ByT5, a byte-level language model. At each outer iteration, LMMSE estimates the channel from known pilots and data symbol feedback, and EP detects the data symbols. ByT5 then maps the data symbol probabilities to byte probabilities, which provide soft symbol statistics and semantic priors for feedback to LMMSE and EP, respectively, in the next iteration. Simulation results show that Sem-JCED requires about 7~dB lower signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) than conventional JCED to reach a bit error rate (BER) of $1\times10^{-2}$ with four users and four receive antennas, and outperforms maximum-likelihood detection with perfect channel knowledge over the simulated SNR range.

title: TP-JSCC: Efficient Token Pruning and Joint Source-Channel Coding for LVLMs-based 3D-VQA in Cloud-Edge Collaboration
authors: Zhengxin Li; Chongzhen Tian; Hui Yuan; Hao Liu; Sam Kwong
abstract: Deploying large vision-language models (LVLMs) on resource-constrained embodied agents for 3D visual question answering necessitates cloud-edge collaboration. However, offloading massive visual data to the cloud over bandwidth-limited and noisy channels introduces severe latency and transmission distortion. To address this, we propose TP-JSCC, an efficient token pruning and joint source-channel coding method for LVLMs-based 3D-VQA in Cloud-Edge Collaboration. First, we develop a Local and Global Semantics-based Hybrid Token Pruning (LGS-HTP) module to significantly reduce the visual token count. By decoupling foreground-background tokens and jointly selecting local and global semantics, LGS-HTP effectively reduces redundancy while preserving reasoning-critical tokens. Second, we introduce a lightweight Token Joint Source-Channel Coding (T-JSCC) module to further compress the pruned tokens and ensure their robust transmission over error-prone channels. By employing lightweight cascaded linear layers and Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR)-adaptive mechanism, this module adapts to fluctuating channel conditions while maintaining minimal computational overhead. Extensive experiments on ScanQA and SQA3D datasets indicate the exceptional efficiency and robustness of our approach. Specifically, on ScanQA validation set, the LGS-HTP module could achieve 90% pruning ratio while incurring less than a 1% CIDEr loss. Building on this, the T-JSCC further compresses the tokens by 18 times, resulting in an overall 180 times data volume reduction for robust transmission, while saving 90% in computational complexity for LVLM deployment. Our code is available at https://github.com/yuanhui0325/TP-JSCC.

title: Many Perturbations, Shared Failure Dynamics: Tracing Direction-Sensitive Perturbation Influence in Language Models
authors: Zhibo Hu; Chen Wang; Yanfeng Shu; Liming Dong; Hye-young Paik; Liming Zhu
abstract: Why can a task-preserving rewrite turn a correct answer into a failure while a larger internal change leaves the answer intact? We develop a direction-sensitive, readout-relative account of semantic fragility: heterogeneous language changes can share geometric and readout relationships without sharing an input-independent failure direction. Clean decision reserve, representation transformation, and response alignment provide complementary descriptions of this process. An exact longitudinal-transverse decomposition identifies directional information discarded by scalar transmission. A compact reserve-and-transmission model predicts failures across held-out families and items in Qwen3-32B and Gemma 4 31B, with useful but parameterization-dependent transfer to ReClor. Matched interventions show that orientation carries causal information beyond scalar geometry. Among naturally failed rewrites, attention-component tests on disjoint original items and subsequent answer-order controls favor the natural paired direction over tested random and same-answer-letter donor directions. Yet failures rarely persist across option orders, and current-order corrections use recomputed clean references. Shared predictive regularity thus coexists with context-dependent directional effects. Numerical path integration reduces, but does not eliminate, finite-patch approximation error within a fixed context; a larger discrepancy from the natural rewrite effect remains. A complementary fixed-CoT cue study extends this account to influence unacknowledged in recorded reasoning: readout associations transfer across domains, although the positive-mean causal criterion fails and signed-effect prediction remains post hoc. Together, these results support shared relations among reserve, transformation, and response while distinguishing local causal sensitivity from a complete explanation of natural failure.

title: Bio-Inspired Auditory Processing: Coupling Parallel Resonate-and-Fire Dynamics with Ternary Recurrent Networks for Speech Recognition
authors: Pavlos Poulos; Katelyn Sadorf; Themos Stafylakis; Costas A. Anastassiou
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) promise energy-efficient inference through sparse, event-driven computation, yet remain constrained on continuous, context-dependent tasks such as automatic speech recognition (ASR). A key bottleneck is the Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neuron, whose membrane decay erases information across pauses and phonetic boundaries while it must both extract features and retain long-range context. Inspired by cortical separation of nonlinear filtering and somatic integration, we introduce the Spiking Ternary GRU (stGRU): a ternary-weight gated recurrent unit performs temporal filtering, while downstream Resonate-and-Fire (RF) neurons generate the binary spike stream driving the next block's event pathway. This makes binary event transmission a native training constraint rather than a separate deployment-time activation quantization step; together with ternary weights, learned projections avoid dense floating-point matrix MACs. Trained end-to-end on LibriSpeech-960, Small, Medium, and Large stGRUs reach 8.09%, 7.04%, and $6.44 \pm 0.17\%$ WER on test-clean without an external language model. To our knowledge, these are the first matrix-MAC-free spiking networks without a learned ANN sequence decoder to achieve single-digit WER on LibriSpeech. The architecture also achieves 10.88% test CER on Aishell-1 (9.28% on dev) when trained from scratch. Internally, trained networks develop a depth-graded hierarchy: shallow layers act as fast acoustic filters, while deep layers form slower semantic integrators whose latent representations segregate into part-of-speech manifolds and word-level spike events. Deep-layer firing rates follow lognormal distributions with a sparsity gradient, mirroring hierarchical processing observed in human cortex in vivo. Our biologically grounded architecture combines competitive ASR with favorable modeled compute and memory cost.

title: Artificial intelligence applications in forensic science and their implications for education and training
authors: María Belén Morales-Cevallos; Canva Byron Ma Lam; Kevin David Dickens Guerrero; Diego Fabián Vique López
abstract: Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming increasingly relevant to forensic practice and has potential applications in forensic education, including evidence interpretation, simulation-based learning, and decision-making. Then, evidence regarding its educational implementation remains fragmented, with limited consensus on pedagogical frameworks and competency development. Methodology A systematic review was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. Studies published between 2020 and 2025 were identified through Scopus, PubMed, and IEEE Xplore. Eligible studies for the primary synthesis were required to include an identifiable forensic educational or training context, an AI-supported educational intervention, or a measured educational/training outcome. Technical studies of AI applications in forensic practice were analyzed separately to identify emerging competency and curriculum requirements. Results Only a limited subset of the retrieved literature directly examined AI within an educational or training context. The available educational evidence addressed areas such as learner skill development, professional training needs, and AI-supported learning activities, but remained heterogeneous and methodologically limited. In contrast, a much larger body of technical forensic AI research demonstrated rapid advances in image analysis, classification, digital forensics, and decision support. These developments identify emerging educational requirements in algorithmic literacy, validation, explainability, bias assessment, data governance, and human oversight. Discussion Current evidence indicates that AI should complement rather than replace human expertise. Effective implementation requires competency-based curricula integrating computational literacy, ethical reasoning, interdisciplinary collaboration, and experiential learning supported by explainable AI. Conclusion Direct empirical evidence supporting AI-enhanced forensic education remains limited. This scarcity represents an important evidence gap. Rapid technical advances nevertheless provide a strong rationale for developing and prospectively evaluating competency-based AI education in forensic curricula.

title: Mechanism Development for the Digital Living Transmission of Embroidery Intangible Cultural Heritage: A Case Study of Rizhao Embroidery
authors: Ping Lin
venue: Journal of Advances in Social Sciences
abstract: Digital technologies have opened up new pathways for the living transmission of intangible cultural heritage (ICH). However, digitalization practices for local traditional crafts generally place greater emphasis on storage and preservation than on transmission and inheritance, and sustainable operational mechanisms have yet to be established. To address the developmental challenges of digital transmission in traditional crafts, this study takes Rizhao embroidery as a case study and employs a case study approach to examine the structural constraints on its digital living transmission from three dimensions: knowledge, participation, and value, drawing on multiple sources of data. The findings reveal a closed-loop constraint in the digital transmission of Rizhao embroidery, characterized by discontinuities in knowledge transformation, the absence of sustained learning mechanisms, and insufficient value feedback and circulation. These three constraints are interrelated and mutually reinforce one another, thereby limiting the long-term transmission of ICH. Building on the essential principles of living ICH transmission, this study develops a three-dimensional operational mechanism and a five-stage transmission model comprising “recording, dissemination, learning, co-creation, and feedback,” thereby clarifying the systemic operational logic of digital living transmission. By moving beyond the conventional perspective of technology-enabled transmission, this study contributes to the theoretical framework for the digital transmission of local traditional crafts and provides a feasible reference model for the digital, living, and sustained transmission of local ICH.

title: DSC-CAN: a cross-attention network with dual-space calibration for RF-based open-set UAV identification
authors: Jianyu Hao; Qiang Kong; Maowei He; Hanning Chen; Yongli An
abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) applications increases the demand for reliable low-altitude airspace monitoring. Radio-frequency (RF)-based UAV identification provides a passive and non-visual solution by exploiting transmitter-dependent signal characteristics. In open-world deployments, an RF monitoring system needs to recognize known UAV emitters while rejecting previously unseen RF signals. However, open-world RF monitoring remains challenging because known UAV signals often exhibit substantial intra-class variations, while unseen signals can lie close to known-class distributions. These factors make it difficult to preserve known-class discrimination and reliably reject unknown signals under resource-constrained deployments. To address these limitations, we propose the Dual-Space Calibrated Cross-Attention Network (DSC-CAN), a parameter-efficient framework for open-set RF UAV identification. We first employ a compact local–global cross-attention encoder to coordinate fine-grained RF patterns and long-range contextual dependencies, thereby learning compact and discriminative representations. We then introduce class-adaptive prototype-radius calibration to construct class-specific acceptance regions from known training and calibration data, enabling adaptive boundary estimation without using unknown test samples. Finally, we develop dual-space geometric fusion to combine Euclidean prototype-distance evidence with contrastive cosine evidence, thereby suppressing unreliable acceptance decisions when the two spaces provide inconsistent support for a known class. Experiments on multiple known–unknown class partitions show that DSC-CAN achieves strong and stable open-set performance with only 0.187 M parameters. In the primary scenario, DSC-CAN obtains an H -score of 0.9542, an AUROC of 0.9847, an FPR@95 of 0.0368, and an OSCR of 0.9586. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of the overall design and the complementary roles of its components.

title: Documenting symptom and context changes in individual case safety reports: a methodological perspective
authors: Eik Niederlohmann
venue: Frontiers in Drug Safety and Regulation
abstract: Individual case safety report narratives support pharmacovigilance by preserving clinical chronology and contextual information. A possible information gap concerns how documented symptom changes, surrounding circumstances, and actions already taken are linked and attributed to their sources. Its frequency and consequences have not been established. This Perspective proposes a minimal representation of symptom trajectories, context, actions, subsequent responses, concurrent changes, and remaining uncertainty. A limited procedural inspiration is the repeated observation and revision of working hypotheses used in dynamic psychotherapy; this does not establish a new pharmacovigilance diagnostic method. The proposal builds on existing case processing, causality frameworks, quality assessment, and follow-up practice. Evaluation would first audit source records and processing histories, then compare the proposed representation with optimized routine narratives containing the same facts. An independently adjudicated reference would specify what the records support, without claiming to establish biological causality. The primary endpoint would be correct reconstruction of prespecified case information; unsupported conclusions, completion, and workload would be assessed separately. Additional questioning would require a later, distinct evaluation of information yield, nonresponse, recall, and questioning effects. Contextual information must not delay reporting or justify unsupported dismissal of a medicinal-product contribution. The representation warrants testing, including the possibility that good routine processing already provides equivalent practical information.

title: Semantic Drift in AI-Native 6G Multi-Agent Systems: A Systematic Review and Taxonomy of Mitigation Strategies
authors: Odesa Ogaga Edward; Afolabi Awodeyi; Ugbeh Raymond Nduka; Omolegho Ibok; Idama Omokaro
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: AI-native sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks are envisioned to orchestrate massive populations of autonomous agents—including unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs), industrial robotics, and distributed Internet of Things (IoT) nodes—that transcend traditional bit-pipe transmissions to exchange rich, task-oriented semantic representations. Extracted via advanced edge artificial intelligence (AI), transmitted across learned air interfaces, fused into shared knowledge bases, and ultimately translated into collaborative joint actions, this semantic processing pipeline is inherently vulnerable to compounding imperfections.Sensors degrade through calibration loss and environmental wear, edge inference models suffer from severe distribution shifts, semantic encoders and decoders experience mutual misalignment, wireless channels distort latent feature spaces, knowledge bases diverge across heterogeneous vendors, and malicious or faulty Byzantine peers inject persistent false beliefs. We formally define the resulting gradual degradation of alignment between representation and reality, as well as inter-agent consensus divergence, as semantic drift.This comprehensive review traces the entire sensing-to-decision pipeline across seven distinct stages(S1→ S7) . We introduce a rigorous stage-wise formalization accompanied by an end-to-end analytical error bound demonstrating how localized errors propagate and amplify downstream. Furthermore, we present a structured detect–prevent–correct–contain taxonomy of mitigation mechanisms for each stage, evaluate numerical models contrasting vulnerable linear consensus with Byzantine-resilient fusion, outline a closed-loop cross-stage management architecture with joint resource allocation formulations, consolidate evaluation metrics, and articulate open research challenges.

title: CrossWeave: Cross-Modal Scene and Instance Retrieval from Sparse 2D-3D Alignment
authors: Aadith Warrier; Gnana Prakash Punnavajhala; Siddharth Tourani; Muhammad Haris Khan; Avinash Sharma; Madhava Krishna
abstract: Cross-modal scene and instance retrieval aims to retrieve a corresponding 3D environment or object given query 2D images, serving as a foundational mechanism for spatial reasoning in robotics and AR/VR. Existing methods achieve this by learning alignment only at the level of whole scenes or objects, which provides no supervision for the fine-grained local structure within them. In this work, we show that supervision on a set of sparse 2D-3D correspondences, without scene- or instance-level contrastive objectives, is sufficient to train a single model for both scene- and instance-level retrieval. Specifically, we propose $\textbf{CrossWeave}$, a novel framework for cross-modal retrieval that learns sparse patch-point alignment, which alone outperforms existing methods. An optimal transport-based aggregator over the aligned features gives further gains by clustering structurally redundant regions, freeing descriptor capacity for semantically distinct local features. CrossWeave achieves state-of-the-art performance on both scene- and instance-level retrieval on ScanNet and 3RScan with a $\textit{single model}$, whereas existing methods require separate models for each task. Our results suggest that whole-scene encoding is unnecessary for cross-modal retrieval and that sparse local correspondence supervision is a more effective and flexible alternative.
